fields.title: Design and Implementation of Deterministic Finite Automaton (DFA)
fields.aim: To design and implement a Deterministic Finite Automaton (DFA) for accepting strings belonging to a specified language.
fields.requirements:
Python 3.x
VS Code / IDLE
Basic knowledge of Python programming
Basic knowledge of Finite Automata
fields.theory:
A Deterministic Finite Automaton (DFA) is a finite state machine used to recognize regular languages.

A DFA consists of five components:

Q = A finite set of states
Σ = A finite input alphabet
δ = Transition function
q0 = Initial state
F = Set of final or accepting states

The transition function of a DFA maps each state and input symbol to exactly one state.

For example, consider a DFA over the alphabet {0, 1} that accepts strings ending with 1.

The DFA contains two states:
q0 – Initial state
q1 – Final state

Transitions:
From q0, input 0 leads to q0.
From q0, input 1 leads to q1.
From q1, input 0 leads to q0.
From q1, input 1 leads to q1.

After processing the complete input string, if the machine is in the final state q1, the string is accepted; otherwise, it is rejected.

DFA is deterministic because for every state and every input symbol, there is exactly one possible transition.
fields.procedure:
1. Define the states of the DFA.
2. Define the input alphabet.
3. Select the initial state.
4. Select the final/accepting state.
5. Define the transition function.
6. Take an input string from the user.
7. Start from the initial state.
8. Read each character of the input string one by one.
9. Move to the corresponding state according to the transition function.
10. After processing the complete string, check the current state.
11. If the current state is an accepting state, display "String Accepted".
12. Otherwise, display "String Rejected".

fields.title: Conversion of NFA to DFA
fields.aim: To design a Non-Deterministic Finite Automaton (NFA) and convert it into an equivalent Deterministic Finite Automaton (DFA).
fields.requirements:
Python 3.x
VS Code / IDLE
Basic knowledge of Python programming
Basic knowledge of NFA and DFA
fields.theory:
A Non-Deterministic Finite Automaton (NFA) is a finite automaton in which a state can have zero, one, or multiple transitions for the same input symbol.

Unlike a DFA, an NFA can have multiple possible next states for a given current state and input symbol.

Every NFA has an equivalent DFA that recognizes the same language.

The standard method used to convert an NFA into a DFA is called the Subset Construction method.

In this method, each DFA state represents a set of NFA states.

For example, if the NFA has states {q0, q1, q2}, possible DFA states may be {q0}, {q0,q1}, {q1,q2}, etc.

The initial DFA state is the set containing the initial NFA state.

A DFA state is considered final if it contains at least one final state of the NFA.

The subset construction method guarantees that the resulting DFA accepts exactly the same language as the original NFA.
fields.procedure:
1. Define the states of the NFA.
2. Define the input alphabet.
3. Define the initial state.
4. Define the final state or states.
5. Define the NFA transition function.
6. Start the subset construction from the initial state.
7. Treat each set of NFA states as one DFA state.
8. Calculate transitions for every input symbol.
9. Continue until no new DFA states are generated.
10. Mark every DFA state containing an NFA final state as a final state.
11. Test the resulting DFA with an input string.
12. Display whether the string is accepted or rejected.

fields.title: Study and Implementation of Virtualization Using VirtualBox
fields.aim: To study the concept of virtualization and create a virtual machine using Oracle VirtualBox.
fields.requirements:
1. Computer/Laptop with minimum 8 GB RAM
2. Windows/Linux operating system
3. Oracle VirtualBox
4. Ubuntu ISO image
5. Basic knowledge of operating systems and virtualization
6. Internet connection for downloading required software
fields.theory:
Virtualization is a fundamental technology used in cloud computing. It allows a physical computer's hardware resources such as CPU, memory, storage and network resources to be shared among multiple virtual machines.

A Virtual Machine (VM) is a software-based computer that runs an operating system and applications independently from the host operating system.

Oracle VirtualBox is a virtualization software that allows users to create and manage virtual machines on a physical computer.

In cloud computing, virtualization provides resource sharing, isolation, scalability and efficient utilization of physical hardware.

A hypervisor is the software layer responsible for creating and managing virtual machines. VirtualBox works as a hosted (Type-2) hypervisor because it runs on top of an existing host operating system.

The basic process of virtualization is:
Physical Machine → Hypervisor → Virtual Machine → Guest Operating System.

Virtualization is widely used in cloud platforms because multiple virtual machines can run on the same physical server.
fields.procedure:
1. Download and install Oracle VirtualBox on the host computer.
2. Download an Ubuntu ISO image.
3. Open Oracle VirtualBox.
4. Click on the New option to create a virtual machine.
5. Enter a suitable name for the virtual machine.
6. Select Linux as the operating system and Ubuntu as the version.
7. Allocate suitable RAM to the virtual machine.
8. Create a virtual hard disk.
9. Select the Ubuntu ISO image as the installation media.
10. Start the virtual machine.
11. Follow the Ubuntu installation instructions.
12. After installation, start the virtual machine.
13. Verify that the guest operating system is running successfully.
14. Observe the CPU, memory and storage resources assigned to the virtual machine.
fields.code:
This practical is based on virtualization software and does not require a programming code.

The implementation is performed using Oracle VirtualBox by creating and running an Ubuntu virtual machine.

fields.title: Study and Implementation of Basic Network Commands
fields.aim: To study and implement basic network commands used for network configuration, connectivity testing and troubleshooting.
fields.requirements:
1. Computer/Laptop
2. Windows or Linux operating system
3. Command Prompt / Terminal
4. Active network connection
5. Basic knowledge of computer networks
fields.theory:
Network commands are useful tools for configuring, monitoring, testing and troubleshooting computer networks.

Some commonly used network commands are:

1. ipconfig – Displays IP address, subnet mask and default gateway information in Windows.

2. ping – Tests connectivity between the local computer and another network device by sending ICMP packets.

3. tracert – Displays the path followed by packets from the local computer to a destination.

4. nslookup – Retrieves DNS information and resolves a domain name into an IP address.

5. hostname – Displays the name of the current computer.

6. arp – Displays and manages the ARP cache, which contains mappings between IP addresses and MAC addresses.

These commands are commonly used by network administrators and developers to diagnose network connectivity and configuration problems.
fields.procedure:
1. Open Command Prompt on Windows or Terminal on Linux.
2. Execute the hostname command and observe the computer name.
3. Execute the ipconfig command to display network configuration.
4. Execute the ping command with a known IP address or domain name.
5. Observe the packets sent, received and lost.
6. Execute the tracert command with a domain name.
7. Observe the different network hops between the computer and destination.
8. Execute the nslookup command with a domain name.
9. Observe the DNS server and IP address information.
10. Execute the arp -a command to display the ARP cache.
11. Record the output of each command.
12. Analyze the information obtained from the commands.
fields.code:
Basic Network Commands:

ipconfig
ping google.com
tracert google.com
nslookup google.com
hostname
arp -a
